newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end lower, Chidambaram yet to speak.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end lower, Chidambaram yet to speak.

text.p: Bombay shares ended lower on Friday when a speech by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on the 1996/97 budget -- expected during market hours -- failed to materialise, traders said.
"Maybe he waited until the market closed because what he's going to deliver will disappoint the market," said a trader at a foreign broking firm.
Some traders said punters who took positions expecting Chidambaram to speak during trading hours may have squared positions ahead of the weekend.
The 30-stocks index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) fell 9.16 points to a provisional close of 3507.74 after hitting an early high of 3543.21.

Chidambaram's statement on the budget has been put off many times this week due to disruption of parliament over a political row. The market expects the government to relax a controversial minimum tax on high-growth firms, scrap double taxation of dividends and raise tax exemption limits on investor incomes.
The finance minister is expected to spell out the tax breaks, if any, only next week when he will make a detailed statement on the finance bill.
The broader CRISIL-500 index fell marginally to a provisional close of 691.37 points against 691.42.
Traders said there were sellers in SBI after news that the bank would launch its GDR issue this month.
"There were some foreign funds selling with the intention of picking up stock from the GDR," one trader said.

Shares of electronics firm Philips fell on prolonged labour problems which have resulted in a two day strike at its unit in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta. Philips shares slid 7.75 rupees to 97.50 on the BSE.
